question: Does a 512-token context-partitioned M16 score-producer/value-consumer decomposition reduce Hopper register residency and tail-wave waste for the exact c32 M384 verifier attention consumer?

hypothesis.causal_change: Separate M16 QK/online-softmax score producers from striped V/output consumers: producers persist BF16 scores plus exact partition max/normalizer state, a small merge forms the global state, and 64-feature consumers read direct paged FP8 V without retaining full-D output accumulators.

predicted_movement.registers_per_thread: offline SM90 CUBIN: local/global score producers 128/239, state merge 24/32, value consumers 168, versus stock 255
predicted_movement.active_warps: increase if the local 128-register producer admits two CTAs and the four-warp 168-register consumers admit more resident work
predicted_movement.l2_hbm_traffic: increase analytically by about 24.9% local and 21.4% global from BF16 score write/read; direct KV bytes remain unchanged
predicted_movement.interval_time: decrease only if shorter live ranges and extra grid supply outweigh score traffic and two extra launches

hypothesis.falsifier: A valid exact-consumer row is numerically invalid or candidate p50 is nonpositive after weighted 50-local/10-global aggregation.

scope.kv_layout: page-size-1 shuffled physical slots addressed through kv_indices
scope.output_consumer: complete attention output square-sum plus comparison with the unchanged stock SGLang consumer

physical_model.roofline_prior: memory/latency limited rather than tensor-compute limited; target execution must decide
physical_model.tma_boundary: The exact page-size-1 shuffled KV consumer requires gather loads and cannot use a contiguous TMA KV transaction. TMA of the small contiguous Q tile cannot offset the dominant gather bytes, so the candidate keeps direct FP8 paged reads and separates score production from striped value consumption.

resource_contract.current_external_boundary: The sole registered H100 is maintenance-bound to predecessor recovery and is not claimable by this project.
